Other triggers and strategies center on emergency/police/location cues, while no threat, appraisal, or memory content connects to animals or snakes. This makes that item look clinically disconnected rather than merely unusual.

issues.explanation: Compulsive cleaning can occur after sexual assault, but in this profile it is not supported by the other selected items or the formulation. The active pattern strongly links triggers, threat, and negative appraisals to maladaptive strategies, yet the listed triggers/threats/appraisals point to hypervigilance, emergency/uniform cues, and situational avoidance rather than contamination, dirtiness, or washing/control themes. As selected here, the cleaning item appears insufficiently connected to the rest of the profile.

vignette: Ahmed is a 54-year-old Middle Eastern man who has been working as a software engineer for over three decades. Since his retirement from work two years ago, Ahmed has increasingly struggled with the memories and aftermath of a sexual assault that occurred during his college years. His experiences have deeply affected his daily life and left him in a state of constant vigilance. The traumatic event took place one evening when he was alone with a male classmate who had been drinking heavily. The perpetrator’s aggressive actions were sudden and brutal, leaving Ahmed feeling violated and utterly helpless. This experience has ingrained specific triggers that still cause intense distress, such as sirens or ambulances passing by, the presence of other men in isolated settings, and anything reminiscent of authority figures in uniform. Ahmed's life since then has been marked by a series of avoidance behaviors that have only deepened his feelings of injustice and self-blame. He avoids locations connected to his trauma, including areas where he once felt safe during his college years, and stays away from places where he might encounter military or police uniforms. His constant scanning for danger leads him to avoid public spaces and crowded environments, as these often trigger false alarms that make him feel like he is in immediate peril. The sirens of passing ambulances remind Ahmed of the emergency services called during his assault, leading him to retreat into his home where he feels a semblance of safety. His avoidance behaviors have only intensified over time; he now refuses to leave his house unless absolutely necessary and avoids any public gatherings or social interactions that might involve men in authority roles. Ahmed's perception of injustice—believing that what happened was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it—has reinforced his maladaptive strategies. He often feels that the world is against him, and this belief makes him further withdraw from society. The constant scanning for danger also exacerbates his sense of self-blame, as he believes his behavior in the past somehow led to the assault. These negative appraisals have created a cycle where Ahmed’s maladaptive strategies, such as avoiding authority figures or any context that reminds him of his trauma, lead to increased feelings of injustice and self-blame. For instance, when he hears sirens, he feels an intense urge to retreat into his safe zone, reinforcing the belief that these contexts are inherently dangerous. Over time, Ahmed’s social circle has dwindled significantly as he avoids interactions with men, even those who were once close friends. His fear of encountering triggers in public places has isolated him from his community and made it difficult for him to engage in simple daily activities like grocery shopping or attending medical appointments. What finally brought Ahmed to seek help was a particularly distressing incident where the sound of an ambulance siren led him into a panic attack, causing him to isolate himself even further. He is most afraid that he will never be able to feel normal emotions again and hopes that therapy can provide a path towards regaining some sense of safety and control in his life. Ahmed’s current state is characterized by intense vigilance and avoidance behaviors, driven by the belief that danger lurks around every corner. The cycle of triggers leading to maladaptive strategies and reinforcing negative appraisals has tightened over time, making it increasingly difficult for him to lead a normal life without feeling constantly on edge.
